title: A story cutscene: a full-screen illustration of a moment the game's own views can't show faithfully (story/cutscenes.gd, docs/ui/cutscenes.md)

title.description: A name for the moment (journal, galleries, tests).

summary.description: What the picture shows and when it plays, in our own words.

images.description: The picture's takes, first match wins: a take whose `when` holds is shown; none holding skips the cutscene.

when.description: A dialogue condition (docs/contracts/dialogue.md); empty is always.

focus.description: Where the picture's slow push-in closes on, as a share of its width and height (default the centre).

once.description: The picture plays only the first time: its trigger's first firing (an area you walk into again and again), or the first time a conversation's `cutscene` statement reaches it.

trigger.description: A Narrator key that plays it while exploring or in a fight (examine:bonegrinder_lookout, strahd:fled_to_coffin): the narrator's line becomes its caption. find:<magic item> plays it when a Tarokka treasure is found, and read:<magic item> when an item's reading plays it (the Tome of Strahd's first reading: the inventory asks Cutscenes.for_trigger). Conversations play cutscenes with the `cutscene <id>` statement instead.

then.description: The scene that follows this one when a trigger plays it (owner rule, 2026-10-14: every cutscene is at least two scenes): another cutscene, with its own picture and a `caption`, fading in over this one after its last caption. Chains.

caption.description: On a scene that another cutscene's `then` names: the Narrator key (scene:<id>, in narrative/narrator/) whose line reads over its picture.

more.description: Further captions over the same picture, after its first (the trigger's line, or `caption`): Narrator keys whose lines read one after another, a click each. The Tome of Strahd's four pictures read three captions each.
